question: is there a real slowdown in 1.1 Nth and count since f9e087e, or are count requests in the post-pass pool noisier than the controls normalise?
command: D44b's recorded set and D48's _hull_refutes (verification/d44b-count-latency-verdict.json at 1fd7204)

rule.i: median <= 1.02 and at most 1 pair above 1.05

variance.note: within: each request's 3 runs in one process (8 pairs x 2 sides = 16 processes); between: over the 8 pairs, the standard deviation of the natural log of each ratio

count_latency_report.windows: each patient's second coded seizure (a seizure record that is not a letter mention), 730 days; no window without one
count_latency_report.p95_note: a p95 over n runs is the ceil(0.95 n)-th smallest: over the 12 runs of a request at one worker count (4 repeats of 3 runs) it is the maximum
count_latency_report.order: ABBA: the reference first in even repeats, the candidate first in odd

absolute.note: D51: 1.3 event frequency not run; D44b's absolute bar not applied

control_structural.changed_set_source: fixed: D44b's recorded set and D48's _hull_refutes (verification/d44b-count-latency-verdict.json at 1fd7204)

count_latency_report.limitations: one machine and one session; synthetic data replicated beyond 10,000 patients; four fixed requests with counts and two without, not a clinical mix; a pair's time is the median of a few runs in one process, so the pairing cancels slow drift, not noise inside a run

count_latency_report_note: the count-latency tool's own report, embedded; its `verdict` is D44b's rule on a subset of requests (its protocol check wants all six), not D51's
